paper_title: Oil-Price Exposure as a Single-Factor Smart-Beta Strategy
summary: Investigate further. The engine tested an adapted experiment based on Oil-Price Exposure as a Single-Factor Smart-Beta Strategy: OILP is each security's slope coefficient b_i,oil from a time-series regression of its returns on monthly simple oil-price changes plus other risk controls, estimated on a training sample. A constrained long-short optimizer builds positive, neutral and negative OILP-target portfolios (maximizing exposure to historical residual returns subject to the OILP target, other factor targets, gross long/short allocations and name bounds); a timing signal s(t) picks positive if s(t) >= h, negative if s(t) <= -h, neutral otherwise, holding the positive-OILP portfolio, conditional on higher contemporaneous or correctly forecast oil returns (no unconditional premium claimed). Historical performance is mixed: net CAGR 15.80% vs 12.83% for the EW universe; Sharpe 0.63 vs 0.66. Robustness is unknown: 10 bps: holds, 25 bps: holds, 0 of 0 evaluated sub-periods hold; 2 not evaluated, group rho 0.92 in the expected direction; alpha t 1.40 (reported, not a gate). Economics are positive: P(NPV > 0) 80%, median incremental fee PV $4.4M vs the EW universe fund. This summary is generated deterministically from the saved results.
